note: ADR-0006 template-owned path boundary. Ownership is resolved by longest matching prefix; a prefix ending in '/' matches a directory subtree, otherwise it matches an exact file. On a tie, user-owned wins (fail-closed: an upgrade never touches a path it isn't sure the template owns). Conservatively excludes apps/ (portal carries user/plugin pages) and infra/environments/ (per-instance config and secrets) for now; that boundary can widen later. services/api/migrations/versions/ is user-owned even though services/api/ is template-owned: Alembic migration files are an append-only, per-instance chain (each instance accumulates its own, chained by down_revision), so syncing them from the template breaks the instance's revision graph. It stays user-owned — the three-way merge must never rewrite an applied migration — but as of issue #198 `biffo core upgrade` runs a separate *additive* carry for it: new core migrations absent from the instance are appended, re-chained onto the instance's current head at upgrade time (and given a deterministic core_<hash> revision id if the template's own id is already taken in that instance), with the resulting chain validated for a single head before the PR is opened. Existing instance migrations are never modified, re-chained, or deleted. See cli/src/lib/core-migrations.ts. The migration framework itself (migrations/env.py, script.py.mako) stays template-owned. services/_plugins/ is template-owned even though services/ is user-owned: it is the carve-out that gives *first-party* plugins a distribution mechanism (issue #243). A plugin shipped in the template (e.g. orchestrator) previously sat directly under the user-owned services/, so `biffo core upgrade` fail-closed on it and the only channel left was manual PR copy-in — which is the absence of a mechanism, and let every instance's copy drift silently. Longest-prefix-wins resolves services/_plugins/ ahead of services/, exactly as services/api/ already does, so the underscore prefix (matching the existing services/_template/ convention, and un-collidable with a kebab-case plugin name per registry-schema.json) is what declares ownership: a plugin under services/_plugins/ is the template's to maintain and is carried by every upgrade, while a third-party plugin installed into services/<name>/ stays the instance's and is never overwritten. Discovery (services/api/src/api/plugins.py) globs both locations, so the split is an ownership boundary only, never a runtime one. apps/ is user-owned, but apps/portal/ within it is wholly template-owned (ADR-0006 longest-prefix wins). The portal is strictly the admin console (issue #306): it serves /admin and /login, the root path belongs to the user's application sibling, and nothing user-owned lives inside it. That portal code is a client of the Core API's admin surface — ~640 lines of *-api.ts calling /api/v1/admin/* — so it tracks the core API's version, not the instance's product. Leaving it user-owned meant template bugs in Biffo's own admin UI could not be distributed: #275 (navigation landing on the raw RSC payload) and #276 (login offering an unsupported identifier) both had to be hand-copied into every instance. #279 part 1 first tried this as a path-level carve-out (app/admin/, app/(auth)/, components/, lib/, context/), which was a trap: components/, lib/ and context/ are exactly where a user would put ProductCard.tsx or stripe.ts, and `core upgrade` would then propose deleting them. #306 removes the trap at its root by making the assumption explicit — the portal is not a canvas — rather than documenting around it, so the carve-out collapses to a single prefix. The instance's own product UI belongs in its application sibling repo, or in a NEW app under apps/, which stays user-owned by default. docs/ADR/ is user-owned: the template's ADRs are seeded once at `biffo init` as a starting point, but an instance's ADRs are its own decision record and legitimately diverge from the Biffo standard over time — force-syncing them on every core upgrade collides an instance's own ADR numbers with the template's and rewrites its history. Excluded from the sync flow for that reason; new template ADRs are announced in release notes rather than pushed into instances. _skeletons/ is template-owned (issue #325). It is scaffolding *source* — the trees `biffo init` (step 6/6), `biffo sibling create` and `biffo plugin create` copy from — not instance content, and no instance ever reads its own copy: the CLI resolves a skeleton by walking UP from its own module (defaultSiblingTemplateRoot() in cli/src/commands/sibling-create.ts, findSkeletonRoot() in cli/src/lib/plugin-scaffold.ts), so an npm-installed CLI lands on the copy packaged beside its own dist/ (cli/scripts/packaged-root-assets.mjs, #315), never on the instance's. The instance has a copy only because `biffo init` clones the whole template repo, and it has been frozen at init time ever since. Leaving it unowned was the #325 trap: cli/ IS template-owned, so the non-interactive-Terraform guard added in #322 (cli/src/lib/terraform-input-guard.ts) was distributed to every instance while the skeleton workflows it scans were not — every upgrade to 0.41.3 landed a guard whose subject the upgrade had no mechanism to fix, and instance CI went red on files the instance neither wrote nor could repair (reproduced on keiranholloway/biffo-platform PR #1). The general rule: a template-owned check must never assert over paths the template does not own. Same argument as services/_plugins/ (#243) — a path the template maintains needs a distribution channel, or it drifts silently in every instance, which is how the #322 bug survived unnoticed in the first place. This is NOT a repeat of the #279 part-1 trap: components/, lib/ and context/ were a trap because they are exactly where a user would put their own ProductCard.tsx or stripe.ts, whereas there is nowhere inside _skeletons/ a user would legitimately add a file. Customising the scaffold is done by pointing `biffo sibling create --template <path>` at your own tree — an explicitly supported flag — not by editing the inherited copy. Making it owned also re-syncs the template-owned tests that read it (cli/src/lib/secret-scan-scope.test.ts, cli/src/adapters/source-control/github/status-checks.test.ts) with their subject, and cli/src/lib/terraform-input-guard.test.ts now asserts every path the guard scans resolves as template-owned, so the mismatch cannot silently return. There is no core.version file to own since issue #423: the version the *template emits* is derived from its core-v* tags, so nothing in the tree names it and there is nothing to sync. The version an instance *received* is recorded in the userOwned biffo.core.json, which is what every lookup reads (cli/src/lib/core-version.ts). Issue #327 (audit follow-up to #325) swept the remaining template-owned checks that asserted over unowned paths and scoped each to template-owned code: the plugin-terraform guard (cli/src/lib/plugin-terraform-guard.ts) now filters discovered manifests through isTemplateOwned so a third-party plugin under user-owned services/<name>/ never reds a template-shipped gate; the CI infra-validate job fmt-checks and terraform-validates only modules/ (never user-owned infra/environments/, whose hardcoded dev env an instance may rename or remove); bandit runs over services/api and services/_plugins only (not the instance's own services/); ruff excludes _skeletons (matching pyright) and db/; and .prettierignore (now template-owned, so the scoping distributes) excludes the user-owned trees the format gate used to reach (apps/ except apps/portal, services/ except the template-owned services, infra/, docs/, README.md, biffo.* config). The general rule is encoded as an executable META guard in cli/src/lib/template-owned-scope.test.ts, with a negative control so it cannot pass by matching its own prose. pnpm-workspace.yaml's apps/* glob is left as-is: enrolling a new user app into the monorepo's shared lint/type/test is the point of a monorepo and the user opts in by creating the app there (the gate fires only on the user's own code, which the user can fix — not the #325 class where the subject is un-fixable inherited content). core-migrations.test.ts's real-tree single-head assertion is now skipped when biffo.core.json is present (i.e. in an instance), so it validates only the template's own shipped chain, never the instance's user-owned migrations/versions/. .husky/commit-msg and .husky/pre-commit are template-owned as EXACT FILES, not the .husky/ directory (issue #370). The template wires the hooks it ships -- commitlint, lint-staged, and the core-ownership guard -- and those wirings must reach instances or the guard exists only in the repo that does not need it. Owning the whole directory would be the #279 part-1 trap in another costume: an instance's own pre-push or post-merge hook is exactly the sort of file a user legitimately adds, and a template-owned subtree would propose deleting it. Exact-file entries own the two hooks the template actually writes and leave the rest of .husky/ to the instance. biffo.divergence.json is user-owned by the same reasoning as the other biffo.*.json files: it records which template-owned prefixes THIS instance knowingly diverges in (warn instead of block), which is per-instance policy the template must never overwrite -- and if it were template-owned, the guard would block the commit that configures the guard. infra/environments/dev/plugins.core.tf is template-owned even though infra/ is user-owned (longest-prefix-wins, same carve-out shape as apps/portal/ inside apps/): it provisions the first-party agentic plugins (orchestrator, agent-runtime) as core capability (ADR-0014), closing #406. The instantiation used to be hand-wired per instance in the user-owned main.tf and drifted — tabsii had it, a fresh instance had nothing and its agents were dead. Making just this file template-owned distributes the wiring and keeps every instance in parity, while leaving the rest of infra/environments/ (per-instance account/domain/secret config) user-owned. It depends only on the template-seeded shape every instance has (var.project_name, local.environment, local.tags, module.events, module.api_gateway) and passes the OpenRouter credential by SSM-path convention rather than a per-instance variable, so it upgrades cleanly into an older instance whose variables.tf never gained the plugin vars. The plugin-allowlist module's core_plugins default lists the same first-party set so those Lambdas reach /api/v1/internal/* with no edit to the user-owned root config; the two lists are kept in step (adding a first-party plugin touches both).
